tools.name: @google/design.md
tools.description: DESIGN.md format, linter, and diff tooling for giving agents a structured visual identity and design-system contract.

commands.name: lint
commands.purpose: Validate a DESIGN.md file against the spec and report contrast, token, and structure findings.

commands.name: diff
commands.purpose: Compare two DESIGN.md files for token-level and prose regressions.

tools.agentUse: Reference when creating or reviewing UI that should follow a persistent visual identity. This is tooling/documentation, not an agent skill.

tools.name: rtk
tools.description: Rust Token Killer: CLI proxy that compresses verbose shell command output before it reaches an LLM context.

commands.name: verify
commands.purpose: Confirm this is Rust Token Killer, not the unrelated Rust Type Kit package.

commands.name: init-claude
commands.purpose: Install global Claude Code hook and RTK.md guidance.

commands.name: init-codex
commands.purpose: Install Codex AGENTS.md and RTK.md guidance.

commands.name: usage-stats
commands.purpose: Show token savings and recent RTK usage history.

tools.agentUse: Use RTK as a shell-output proxy for verbose commands like git status, git diff, test runners, package managers, Docker, and Kubernetes. Do not use it for commands where raw output is explicitly required.

tools.name: codeburn
tools.description: Local dashboard and reporting CLI for visualizing AI coding token usage, cost, providers, models, projects, and task categories.

commands.name: dashboard
commands.purpose: Open the interactive token/cost dashboard.

commands.name: status
commands.purpose: Show a compact today/month usage summary.

commands.name: report-json
commands.purpose: Export structured usage data for analysis.

commands.name: optimize
commands.purpose: Find token waste and setup improvements.

commands.name: models
commands.purpose: Generate a paste-friendly model usage and cost table.

tools.agentUse: Use CodeBurn when the user asks about AI token usage, cost, model comparisons, expensive sessions, or token waste. It is an observability/reporting tool, not a skill.

tools.name: gnhf
tools.description: Good Night, Have Fun: an agent orchestrator for bounded, long-running coding loops while the user is away.

commands.name: verify
commands.purpose: Confirm the installed CLI and inspect supported flags before launching a run.

commands.name: hands-off-run
commands.command: gnhf --max-iterations 10 --stop-when "relevant checks pass and no unrelated files changed" "<objective>"
commands.purpose: Start a bounded overnight-style coding run with a concrete stop condition.

commands.name: worktree-run
commands.purpose: Run a GNHF worker in an isolated git worktree so the main checkout stays clean.

tools.agentUse: Use GNHF when the user asks for a long-running, agent-managed coding loop, overnight work, or supervised iterative work. Keep stop conditions concrete and independently verify results before acceptance.

tools.name: code-review-graph
tools.description: Local knowledge graph for AI coding tools. Builds a structural map of your codebase with Tree-sitter for precise context and 6-8x token reduction on reviews.

commands.name: install
commands.purpose: Auto-detect and configure all supported AI platforms (Codex, Cursor, Claude Code, etc.)

commands.name: build
commands.purpose: Parse entire codebase into the graph database

commands.name: review-delta
commands.purpose: Review changes since last commit with blast-radius analysis

commands.name: visualize
commands.purpose: Generate interactive HTML graph or export to GraphML/SVG/Obsidian

commands.name: daemon-start
commands.purpose: Start multi-repo watch daemon for automatic graph updates

tools.agentUse: Use code-review-graph when working with large codebases where token efficiency matters. The graph provides blast-radius analysis, semantic search, and minimal-context queries via MCP. Particularly useful for code reviews and navigating monorepos.

tools.name: autoskills
tools.description: CLI for automatically discovering and applying relevant agent skills from the current context.

commands.name: run
commands.purpose: Run autoskills through npx to inspect context and surface useful skills.

commands.name: repo-wrapper
commands.purpose: Use this repo's convenience wrapper for npx autoskills.

tools.agentUse: Use autoskills when the user wants automatic skill discovery or a quick context-aware skill recommendation pass.
